definitions.explanation: Extremely steep and rising sharply, typically describing mountains, cliffs, slopes, or terrain.

examples.japanese: {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{山道|やまみち}を{登|のぼ}った。
examples.english: We climbed a steep mountain path.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{地形|ちけい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This area has a lot of steep terrain.

examples.japanese: {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{崖|がけ}がそびえ{立|た}ち、{下|した}を{見|み}ると{足|あし}がすくんだ。
examples.english: A sheer cliff towered above, and looking down made my legs freeze.

notes:
A compound of {急|きゅう} (steep/sudden) and {峻|しゅん} (towering/precipitous). Describes terrain that is not merely steep but dramatically so — nearly vertical cliffs, extremely steep mountain faces, or rugged highland terrain. More literary and emphatic than the common {急|きゅう}な.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{山|やま}: steep mountain
- {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{斜面|しゃめん}: steep slope
- {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{崖|がけ}: sheer cliff
- {急峻|きゅうしゅん}な{地形|ちけい}: rugged terrain

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {険|けわ}しい: steep, rugged — the most common everyday word for steep terrain
- {急|きゅう}な: steep, sudden — general-purpose, less dramatic
- {切|き}り{立|た}った: sheer, precipitous — describes a cliff that drops straight down
- {峻険|しゅんけん}: steep and rugged — literary synonym, nearly interchangeable
